newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close flat after hectic rise.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close flat after hectic rise.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed flat on profit-taking, following two days of sharp gains when the all-share index broke through the landmark 750-point barrier, brokers said.

The all-share index closed 0.20 points higher at 773.8 as price gains and declines ran virtually neck and neck at 36 to 32. Commercial Bank rose four rupees to 220, Development Finance three to 275. National Development Bank fell six to 235, Richard Pieris & Co seven to 143.
"Profit-taking was led by retailers, since there was about 10 percent profits to take in most of the stocks," said Dimuthu Abeysekera of Allied Phillips Securities.

Turnover was 71.1 million rupees, led by 100,000 Colombo Dockyard, 250,00 Grain Elevators, 73,600 Tea Services and 120,000 Tea Smallholder. Foreign buying was worth 14.3 million rupees and selling, 6.2 million.
"The buying should continue next week too," said Dihan Dedigama of brokerage John Keells. "But profit-taking should control the index to some extent."
Colombo stocks rose sharply this month after analysts upgraded market earnings, based on good growth expected in 1997 and 1998.
Trading in Kotagala Plantations was suspended pending disclosure of news on a subsidiary, the stock exchange said.
